🌍 US faces serious constraints in military action against Iran: IRGC Advisor

📌 Bandar Abbas, IRNA – Brigadier General Mohammad-Reza Naghdi, a senior adviser to the commander of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC), says that the United States faced serious constraints in military action against Iran, while economic pressure and internal divisions remained central to Washington’s strategy.

At a workers martyrs’ commemoration in Hormozgan Province on Monday, Naghdi said a ground invasion was beyond US capabilities and a naval attack would expose American warships to heavy risks.
​
Airstrikes, he said, were the only remaining military option, but any attack on Iran’s vital infrastructure would trigger retaliation. He added that US threats against energy facilities had receded after Iran warned of a response.
​
Naghdi said Washington hoped sanctions would undermine public confidence, deepen divisions and pressure officials into hasty decisions.
​
He called for national unity, saying workers and industry had a major role in countering pressure through increased production.
​
Iran, he said, had agricultural, industrial, energy, mineral and technical resources to meet more needs domestically. He cited estimates that 90 to 95 percent of medicines and medical equipment could be produced locally, while about 90 percent of food needs were met at home.
​
He called for expanding downstream industries, curbing nonessential imports and developing banana production in Sistan and Baluchestan through irrigation and water-transfer projects. Naghdi described production and construction work as holy struggle.

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iran will respond to any act of aggression against the Islamic Republic without geographical limitations, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Major General Mostafa Izadi says.

Speaking at the third edition of the Omid Media Cup on Sunday, Izadi said Iran has never initiated aggression or a preemptive war but would stand firmly against any attack on the Islamic Republic and the Islamic Revolution.
​
“The Islamic Republic of Iran has announced that, if necessary, it will extend the scope of its confrontation with threats beyond the regional level, and this has also been demonstrated in recent developments,” it said.
​
Referring to the assessment of strategic analysts, the senior commander said the Iranian Armed Forces during the Ramadan War brought about significant changes in the region’s political and geographical equations.
​
Izadi also pointed to developments in Yemen and the role of resistance forces in the Bab el-Mandab Strait, saying, “Developments in this region and the role played by Yemen’s resistance forces are among the issues that have affected the region’s security and military equations.”
​
Elsewhere in his remarks, Izadi described the Armed Forces as one of the main pillars of the Islamic Republic’s power, saying that despite attacks on some military and defense facilities, “our capabilities and readiness in missile production and the defense industries have increased.”
​
He also emphasized the media’s role in explaining the values and ideals of the Islamic Revolution, describing it as a movement that goes beyond political and material transformation and paves the way for human advancement and a brighter future.
